hasyncVersion.note: #459 audited every endpoint sharing OSPFv3's `Response json.RawMessage` envelope pattern and left this one unwrapped deliberately, not for lack of a body type to point at. hasyncVersionResponse.Response is genuinely polymorphic on the wire: an object ({"firmware":{...}}) only when HA is configured and the peer answers; a bare JSON boolean (`false`) on the overwhelming majority of installs (single-node, HA unconfigured — see HasyncStatusController.php's exception path); JSON null on some error paths. Reflecting through it as an object would misdescribe the common case as a schema conflict rather than widen an unverified path, which is the opposite of what #459 is for. PRUNE TRIGGER: if a future OPNsense release collapses this to one shape, or if per-field polymorphic kinds are ever supported by FieldKind, register an envelopeDescent here like the other FRR/Tor endpoints.

required.exercise: Two OPNsense boxes on the isolated testbed bridge with hasync pointed at each other (System > High Availability > Settings: synchronize-to-IP = the peer, plus a shared XML-RPC account holding page-all on BOTH nodes - the account is authenticated on the box being CALLED, so it has to exist on both or the endpoint answers {"response":"Authentication failed"} rather than throwing). This endpoint makes a LIVE XML-RPC call to the peer on every poll, so the peer must be up: stop the second VM, or drop its bridge link, and "response" disappears entirely - the controller returns the exception envelope {"status":"error","message":"fetch error. remote host down? ..."} instead. Boot the second VM before treating a regression here as drift.
required.verified: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-28 (#460), the first time this endpoint has ever answered from a real HA peer. Both boxes returned a populated response object carrying base/firmware/kernel sub-objects, with firmware holding the peer's version and _my_version holding the local one. BOTH branches of the comparison were observed: the peer was first an identical clone (match) and was then switched to the previous stable release channel while the first box stayed on devel (mismatch), so opnsense_hasync_remote_version_match was seen as 1 and as 0. Stays flagged opaque because hasyncVersionResponse.Response is json.RawMessage -> KindAny and is deliberately NOT unwrapped (see the note below), so the canary can only ever prove the key exists - the inner field evidence is this note plus the hasync_test.go fixtures, not a machine assertion.

quaggaOspfInterface.note: #459 audited every endpoint sharing OSPFv3's `Response json.RawMessage` envelope pattern; this one is deliberately left as a bare envelope rather than unwrapped. frr.go's FetchFRROSPFInterfaces decodes TWO candidate shapes for the same endpoint: FRR>=8 wraps per-interface data in {"interfaces": {...}} (frrOSPFInterfaceWrapped, confirmed live against this box's FRR 10.3), while older FRR returns the flat per-interface map directly at the top level (frrOSPFInterfaceEntry map) per the plugin's own doc comments — but that flat shape has never itself been confirmed live. Registering an envelopeDescent requires naming ONE Inner type; picking the wrapped shape would silently assert the flat shape doesn't exist, and picking the flat shape would misdescribe the one shape actually verified. PRUNE TRIGGER: confirm which shape(s) a live box in the support window actually sends (dev-box FRR is 10.3, already wrapped-only), then register an envelopeDescent — same treatment as quaggaOspfv3Interface below, which has no such ambiguity.

keaLeases6.note: DHCPv6 lease rows were the last source-derived Kea surface; closed 2026-07-25. ROOT CAUSE of the long-standing gap, recorded so it is not re-investigated: the Proxmox host kernel is booted with ipv6.disable=1, so /proc/sys/net/ipv6 does not exist in ANY namespace on that host and NO LXC on it can ever run a DHCPv6 client. This is a host-kernel property, not container privilege - the earlier #227 conclusion. Only a VM (own kernel) can hold a v6 lease; bridge-level L2 forwarding is unaffected. REGRESSION TRIGGER: these rows expire within the lease lifetime (~4000s) if that VM is stopped. Also note keaLeases4 is currently EMPTY (no DHCPv4 client on the test VLAN) despite a 2026-07-13 capture, so a v4 lease row is now the weaker side.

required.exercise: Two OPNsense boxes sharing one L2 segment (the isolated testbed bridge), each carrying the SAME CARP VIP - same address, same vhid, same password - with DIFFERENT advskew so the split is deterministic rather than a race: the lower skew wins MASTER, the higher sits BACKUP. Flip them with POST api/diagnostics/interface/carp_status/maintenance on the master; it TOGGLES, so posting it once enters maintenance and fails over, and posting it again leaves maintenance and fails back. A single-node box can only ever report MASTER, so the BACKUP branch of parseCARPStatus needs the second box.
required.verified: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-28 (#460): MASTER on one box and BACKUP on the other simultaneously, swapped across a maintenance-mode failover, then swapped back on failback - so opnsense_carp_vip_status was observed as both 1 and 0 on both boxes. INIT (2) was NOT observed and is not ledgered: it is a sub-second transient a poll-interval scrape is unlikely to ever catch.

carpStatus.note: REACHED 2026-07-28 by #460. The endpoint was always populated on the single-node testbed - one CARP VIP existed - but every interesting VALUE was pinned: status could only be MASTER, advskew could only be 0, demotion could only be 0 and maintenancemode could only be false. The second OPNsense makes all four vary, which is why these are ledgered now rather than when the endpoint first answered. LIVE ANSWER to the rows[].mode question the carpStatus note in exemptions.json parks for #457: mode is served as the string "carp" and is REDUNDANT, not a VIP-type discriminator. get_vip_status returns vhid-bearing CARP VIPs only - the devel box also carries an ipalias VIP on the loopback and it does NOT appear in rows at all - so mode is constant for every row this endpoint can ever emit, and belongs in carpStatus.knownExtraPaths beside vhid_txt. SECOND CORRECTION to that same note: it claims carp.status_msg "only appears in the 'no CARP interfaces configured' case". That is WRONG. status_msg was present as an empty string in all twelve captures taken across MASTER, BACKUP, maintenance and failback on two boxes that each had a configured VIP. It is always present, and merely empty when there is nothing to say. REGRESSION TRIGGER: stop the second VM and status pins back to MASTER and advskew to 0 on the survivor. The paths stay verified but stop VARYING, which no canary can detect - only this note.

keaLeases4.note: CLOSED 2026-07-28 by #460. ROOT CAUSE of the long-standing empty lease list, recorded so nobody re-investigates it: the traffgen LXC held a STATIC address, so nothing on the Kea-served VLAN ever asked for a lease. Switching it to DHCP was NOT sufficient on its own - the legacy ISC dhcpd had restarted and was wildcard-binding UDP/67, silently starving kea-dhcp4 of its socket, so DHCPDISCOVER drew no offers at all. Stopping dhcpd and restarting Kea produced an offer immediately. This is the same dhcpd-versus-Kea collision recorded on 2026-07-13, and it recurs because dhcpd is only STOPPED, never disabled in config. REGRESSION TRIGGERS, likeliest first: (1) the firewall reboots and brings dhcpd back, re-breaking Kea DHCPv4 - check that kea-dhcp4 and not dhcpd owns UDP/67 before calling this drift; (2) the lease expires if the traffgen LXC stops renewing.
